title: Gov't exec tapped to appear in Sara Duterte trial seeks reschedule of testimony
summary: One of the four witnesses expected to testify in the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has requested that the impeachment court allow her to appear on another date.

blocks.text: One of the four witnesses expected to testify in the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has requested that the impeachment court allow her to appear on another date.

At the start of the hearing, presiding officer Senator-judge Francis Escudero said Rowena Mendoza, an official of the Center for International Expositions and Missions (CITEM), has received the subpoena from the impeachment court but requested that she be allowed to testify on another day.
Escudero said they will issue a decision on Mendoza's request before the lunch break.
Mendoza is expected to testify on communications between CITEM and Cale88 concerning food expositions.
Cale88 is one of the businesses declared in Duterte's Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN).
House prosecutor Joel Chua said Mendoza formally informed them that she would not be able to attend because she was overseas.
However, Chua clarified that Mendoza was not withdrawing from the proceedings and said she could testify on another date.
Mendoza did not specify when she would be available, Chua said.
Three other witnesses expected to testify for Duterte's defense are:

items: former Anti-Money Laundering Council officer Atty. Rainer dela Fuente
Department of Trade and Industry Undersecretary Seferino Rodolfo
Food and Drug Administration official Marilyn Pagayunan

blocks.text: Meanwhile, Duterte’s defense counsel Michael Poa said the defense would present four witnesses this week, followed by another batch of five to six witnesses in December.
He said the five to six witnesses in December would most likely be the defense's final batch.
"We don't see the point of prolonging it further. Lalo na kung ayaw naman natin sinasayang din yung oras ng court. We’ll see," Poa told reporters in an ambush interview.
Asked whether Duterte herself would take the witness stand, Poa said the defense would decide depending on how the trial progresses.
He added that the defense would have to file a manifestation before any such appearance. —AOL, GMA News
